summary: Calvert Watkins was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Harvard, the École Pratique des Hautes Études, and the Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies. He held professorships at Harvard (1959–2003) and the University of California, Los Angeles (2003–2013).
Cameron Bailey works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Indiana University, Florida State University under Bryan J. Cuevas, and the University of Oxford under Ulrike Roesler.

Cameron David Warner is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Harvard University, where he studied under Yudru Tsomu, and has held posts at Middlebury College and Dickinson College.
Cameron Kyle Bender Foltz is a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies who completed an MA at Florida State University under Bryan J. Cuevas (attested 2018).

Camillo Alessio Formigatti is an Indologist and Tibetologist who studied at the University of Milan. He worked on the Sanskrit Manuscripts Project at Cambridge (2011–2014), taught at SOAS, and served as Sanskrit Librarian at the Bodleian Library (attested 2019).

Carel Gabriel Cobet was a Dutch scholar of linguistics who studied at Gymnasium Haganum and Leiden University (~1832–1840). He spent his career as a professor at Leiden University in 1846 and from 1849 to 1884.

Carl A. P. Ruck is a scholar of religious studies and archaeology who studied at the University of Michigan (~1956–1960) and Harvard University (~1960–1965). He held a post at Boston University around 1970.

Carl Bielefeldt is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who earned his PhD from UC Berkeley. He studied with Shunryu Suzuki and Seizan Yanagida, and served on the editorial board at Stanford University (~1980–2017).

Carl Cappeller was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Franz Bopp and Albrecht Weber in Berlin, and earned degrees from Leipzig and Jena. He was appointed professor at the University of Jena in 1875.
Carl Christian Rafn was a Danish scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Copenhagen from approximately 1814 to 1816 and later held a post there.
Carl Darling Buck was an American linguist who studied at Yale University (~1882–1889) and Leipzig University (~1889–1892). He served as a professor at the University of Chicago from 1892 to 1933.
Carl Gaedicke was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who earned his PhD from the University of Jena in 1877, studying under Berthold Delbrück, Eduard Sievers, and Carl Cappeller.

Carl Gustav Jung was a Swiss psychologist and religious studies scholar who earned a medical degree from the University of Basel (1895–1900). He held posts at Zurich (~1905–1914), ETH Zurich (1933–1942), and the University of Basel (1944).
Carl Olson is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied under mentor John Y. Fenton. He held the Teacher-Scholar Chair in the Humanities at Allegheny College (attested 2005–2015).

Carl Paul Caspari was a scholar of linguistics and religious studies who studied at Leipzig University under Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer and at Humboldt University of Berlin. He held positions as Lektor (1847) and professor (1857) at the University of Oslo.
Carl Schuster was a scholar of archaeology and Sinology. He completed his studies at Harvard University (~1924–1930) and the University of Vienna (~1931–1934).
Carl Shigeo Yamamoto is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Virginia under the doctoral supervision of Jeffrey Hopkins and David Germano.

Carl Siegfried was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Bonn, Halle-Wittenberg, and under Albrecht Weber and Rudolf von Roth. He was Professor of Sanskrit at Trinity College Dublin (~1855–1860) and later held a post at Jena (~1874–1903).

Carl W. Ernst is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at Stanford and Harvard. He taught at Pomona College (1981–1992) before serving as professor at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (1992–2022).

Carl Wilhelm Vollgraff was a scholar of archaeology and linguistics who earned a doctorate at Berlin. He served as professor of Greek language and literature at the University of Groningen (1908–1916) and Utrecht University (1917–1946).
